**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable TTY allocation before comparing the query result**

With the default Docker Compose execution path, a populated database can now be classified as empty: the `exec` call above omits `-T`, and [Compose documents](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/exec/) that commands “allocate a TTY by default.” TTY output uses CRLF, so command substitution leaves `t\r`; `xargs` does not remove that carriage return, making this comparison fail. Testing this function with mocked successful query output returns 0 for `t\n` but 1 for `t\r\n`. Consequently, `database_wait` offers to restore an already-populated database, exits if restoration is declined, and keeps waiting after restoration because subsequent checks still fail. Add `-T` to the query execution or explicitly strip carriage returns before comparing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
